font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-align: left;\"\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times; font-size: medium;\"\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINT\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"font-size: 15px;\"\u003E :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EA 27 year old male resident of dachenpally working as a designer in printing press presented with the complaints of -\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E1) Headache since 5 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E2) fainting episodes since last 5 years - last episode was 10 days back.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times; font-size: medium;\"\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"font-size: 15px;\"\u003E :\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EThe patient was asymptomatic 4 years back then he met with a RTA bike to bike collision in which he fell on the divider and impact was on his occipital region, as soon as he fell he had an episode of seizure. Many months after this episode he developed headache which was sudden on onset, gradually progressive. He explained it as pulsating type and starts from occipital region and radiates till frontal lobe. The headache is not associated with nausea and vomitings. It’s aggravates on climbing stairs ,lifting heavy weights and waking for long distances and is relived in some hours spontaneously.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EFainting episodes which were about 1 or 2 in a year since 5 years. His reason of admitting to our hospital was one such attack which he got 10 days back and lead to unconsciousness (syncopial attack ? ).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EH\/o palpitations since 1 year associated with sweating. He first felt the palpitation around 1 year back and went to the hospital to get diagnosed where his reports came normal and indicated by doctors as stress related. He was prescribed pranolol BD taking which his symptoms got relived after 3-4 days. Then he again came across palpitations in feb this year for which he visited our hospital and the diagnosis was same as above.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EH\/o stomach pain in left quadrant of stomach ( left hypochondirium ) and Epi gastric region since 1 and half year which was of burning type and aggravated just after taking food and got relived after 1-2 hours.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EH\/o of occasional bleeding per anus which he described as due to body heat and dehydration.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EOn a whole the patient during the whole of history taking just pointed out on just three symptoms again and again which where headache stomach pain and palpitations. There was no particular order in their occurance but they would always be accompanied together whenever the patient felt uneasy.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times; font-size: medium;\"\u003EPAST HISTORY\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"font-size: 15px;\"\u003E :\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003ENot a known case of diabetes,htn,epilepsy,tb or asthama.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EThe patient has a history of RTA 4 years back where he was hit by a speeding vehicle coming from opposite side. He felt on the divider with his occipital region as the area of impact. He felt unconscious for about 2 hours and was shifted to hospital during this time. He was said to have issues in any of the reports and was discharged a day after.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EHe got contracted with COVID-19 in JAN 2022 and got treated at home.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times; font-size: medium;\"\u003EFAMILY HISTORY\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"font-size: 15px;\"\u003E :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EHe has no family history of DM OR HTN OR ANY OF ABOVE MENTIONED PROBLEMS.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EHe is survived by his mother sister and grandmother. His guardian at the hospital was his paternal uncle.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EUpon enquiry I got to know that the patients father passed away at the age of 46years 3 years back due to low heart rate which was around 40-50 bpm usually.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times; font-size: medium;\"\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"font-size: 15px;\"\u003E:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EDiet - mixed during childhood became vegan in his teens\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EAppetite - Decreased appetite since 1 year ( only lunch and dinner consumed ).\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #757575;\"\u003ESleep - Disturbed Sleep\u0026nbsp;due to thoughts.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EBowel and badder movements - normal\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003ENo addictions.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EPatient works at a printing press run by his family which was started by his great granddad. Patient studied till 10 class after which he felt ill and was unable to take his intermediate exams and left his studies. Irrespective of his studies he used to be regular at the printing press and continued so on after discontinuing his studies.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EPatient is an introvert has no friends outside his family and when asked about friends he mentioned his 2 cousins with whom he is close.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EThe patient is an emotional person as any negative\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"font-size: 15px;\"\u003E \u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003Eor bad issues happening around him affected his mind and it starts occupying his mind and is the ignition key to his headches. He is a overthinker. His family is a happy go lucky one and doesn’t have him pestered for anything. Patient has no individual or personal life outside home.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EHe himself described to me that whenever he gets headaches or giddiness he calls his uncle and accompanies with him to the hospital but by the time he reaches the hospital his condition becomes better as he has a good conversation about his thoughts on the way.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial;\"\u003EAll the syncopial attacks happened when he was on his own or alone.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: #757575; normal; margin: 0px; text-transform: uppercase;\"\u003EMY EXPERIENCES WITH GENERAL CELLULAR AND NEURAL CELLULAR PATHOLOGY IN A CASE BASED BLENDED LEARNING ECOSYSTEM'S CBBLE\u003C\/h3\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHello,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is S MD ZIAUDDIN. Currently pursuing my final year of MBBS.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMedical study is very fascinating with endless new things to learn from. The human body is a temple of all kinds of emotions and biochemistries and disturbances in their ecosystem or balance leads to diseased state.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETo me studying medicine was a goal from my childhood and with increasing age I was intrested more and more in this holistic approach towards human body and it's behaviour. Whenever I used to see a prescription I used to go through the medicines prescribed and know their uses like as simple as for what are they used ex: paracetamol for fever, citrizine for allergies and so on. But as I started my medical journey it attracted me more towards the bodies functioning it's way of reaction towards outside world and so on.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EComing to my final year to be honest due to some medical issues of my own and some personal stuff going on in life I was never regular to college so had missed out a lot on case taking and it's application.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAs the course came to its end I started attending regular case scenarios and our GENERAL MEDICINE department made it more easy for me by making learning groups online portfolios to learn from. We were asked to get involved into interactions with esteemed doctors our own PG's professors and mainly our HOD SIR.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWithout any inhibitions I was able to message them any time to clear up my doubts and they were there to assist me and guide me.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWith the help mentioned above am now at a stage where I can take a case on my own and also apply the medical aspect of learning towards medical learning. Am more confident now about my approach towards case taking and application.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMy first encounters,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAs of my first encounter I used to just go through the cases which my friends used to make and learn about it each and every aspect I would search online or learn from my professors and the interaction groups made by our HOD sir\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThen as I became confident with my cases\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI proceeded towards my first case.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt was a 88 years old male with chief complaints of hearing loss with heaviness.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMy first impression as soon as I saw the patient was he was very old but yet was very active. He was resting in the genral ward I was unable to trace him so I shouted for his name and he reacted to it very actively and within fraction of seconds got up and say on the bed. I was amused to see his active nature.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAs I continued with my case taking I got to know that he is a farmer by occupation and was very active in farming. With time he developed hearing loss in his right year which was very recent. But in my view his ability to hear was good only but I guess it might have diminished.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAs I asked what were his chief complaints I discovered a new complaint that was pains in his joints. He was unable to walk without the support of a cane and this made him feel dependent on the cane for movement.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThought ought examination of his joints and the location of pains showed restricted joint movements but were of minimal extent. He was referred for xray and other investigations. And at the end of my interaction with him I gave him a hope of betterment and that he will be well soon, this made the patient smile and he thanked me again and again. I felt very happy and overwhelmed after his reaction.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/smdziauddin203.blogspot.com\/2022\/12\/88-year-old-male-with-chief-complaints.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/smdziauddin203.blogspot.com\/2022\/12\/88-year-old-male-with-chief-complaints.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis case taking made me more confident and I started actively participating in case taking and it's presentation as blogs.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThen recently I was given an opportunity to take a telephonic case which was referred by my HOD sir. Here the task was to interact with the patient on phone and take down his history and case taking.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient was from West bangal.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe case was 52 years old male with htn diabetes and low back ache.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUpon interacting with the patient I discovered many things for example he had a job which required him to sit for long duration of hours and he had to deal with his sons medical condition which influenced his economical and emotional condition.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAfter the case was taken he was carefully guided and followed up for about 2 weeks in which his diet was being checked on regular basis and also the medications which were prescribed to him.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAfter this 2 weeks of span hus reports were very good as he had improved well metabolically and showed a good prognosis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/smdziauddin203.blogspot.com\/2023\/05\/52-years-male-with-hypertention.html?m=1\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/smdziauddin203.blogspot.com\/2023\/05\/52-years-male-with-hypertention.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe above 2 experiences of mine teached me a lot about medicine and human beings.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere is now no limit to patient doctor communication as technology has advanced and it is the way we doctors communicate with the patients brings about a lot of change in our case taking follow up and prognosis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is because it influences the patients mood and emotions towards us and his ability to share his life issues and experiences with us. So more the patient feels comfortable more good will be our case report and our ability to understand his case.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe smile and the happiness of the patients at the time of their discharge or when they feel a positive change in their condition boosts my morale and the doctor in me becomes more passionate and focused towards helping the humanity and bringing about a change in their lives.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAt last I would like to say our profession here is termed noble as it requires a lot of humanity kindness patience and our shear will to help the individuals who come for our help.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThese experiences of mine in this online learning portfolios, group interactions and the support of my PGs SRs and HOD SIR made me a more focused confident doctor and am very thankful to them for what am today.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is just the start there is more to learn and apply in the life of medicine.\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/smdziauddin203.blogspot.com\/feeds\/6280313136151103105\/comments\/default","title":"Post font-family: \u0026quot;open sans\u0026quot;;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINT -\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1] Generalized weight loss since 7 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2] Feeling less energetic since 7 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3] Facial dullness since 2 years\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4] Mid back pain 8 months\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E5] Tail bone pain 7 months\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS -\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient of apparently asymptomatic 7 years back then he noticed a gradual weight loss which was generalized throughout the body. he also experienced thirstiness, generalized weakness and frequently felt hungry. for this he went to the doctor and got diagnosed with diabetes type 2 for which he was prescribed METFORMIN HCL 1000 mg which he takes usually before breakfast.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E8-9 months back he developed lower back pain of the left side which was shooting and radiating type till the hamstring muscles. for this he went to nearby doctor and was prescribed TAB. NEUROKIND ? which he took for about one and a half month. and he got relieved using this medication within 15 days and he completed the course of one and a half month.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E6 months back he developed pain in his tailbone which aggravated on prolonged sitting. for this he got advised to use a physio pillow after using which his pain got diminished. but without the use of this pillow or sitting on hard surfaces the pain aggravates.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2 years back the patient and the people around him noticed a marked change in his facial appearance which he describes as facial muscle loss and loose facial skin. this has effected the patients self confidence and his ability to mingle with people as he was always pointed out about how his face had become less attractive and dull.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EApart from the above mentioned issues his concentration has decreased in his general office work from past 1 year.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPAST HISTORY -\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient is a known case of DM TYPE 2 since 7 YEARS for which he takes METFORMIN HCL 1000mg OD\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient is a known case of HYPERTENTION since 5YEARS for which he takes OLMESARTAN which was of the following doses -\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E20mg - first 2 years\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E40mg- next 3 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E20mg -from this march 2023.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient got involved in a road traffic accident 7 years back in which he had a patella fracture and muscle tear in his lower mid back which got healed over time. upon general checkup 2 years back the issues were said to be resolved and healed,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr
